cohort: 476 mothers who underwent cesarean section between January 1st and December 31st, 2018 at public hospitals in Dire Dawa administration; 119 cases with post-cesarean section surgical site infection and 357 controls
finding: Increased maternal age, a higher number of vaginal examinations, history of chorioamnionitis, previous cesarean section, not receiving antibiotics prophylaxis, lower perioperative hematocrit level, and longer duration of membrane rupture were independently associated with post-cesarean section surgical site infection.
